concept.title: Components
concept.shortdesc: Exploring what components go into a desktop PC

conbody.p: A desktop PC consists of several parts. The bare minimum for a working computer is a central processing unit, motherboard, random access memory, power supply unit, and a monitor and keyboard for interaction. In practice though you will want a case to put everything in, a storage device, and an operating system. Graphics and networking cards will round out your machine’s capabilities.

Components are presented in approximate order of importance to your build. Your choice of CPU will determine what motherboard you need, and those two components are the core of your build. The next most important part is the graphics card, followed by the RAM. Networking cards, storage, and the case are vital but are rarely major choice points. The PSU is presented last of the major components not because it is least, but because you’ll need to know your total wattage requirements from every other part before selecting it.
